findings.title: Task 6 breaks `tests/tools/test_package.py` and no task updates it
findings.description:
- **What breaks:** `test_exactly_the_three_builtin_tools_are_registered` asserts `set(tools.list_tools()) == {"read_file", "write_file", "bash"}` (line 11). `test_materialize_binds_every_registered_tool` asserts `len(executors) == 3` (line 22). Task 6.4 registers five more tools at import, so both fail the moment Task 6 lands.
- **Why the plan misses it:** Task 6 has no scoped test command, and Task 7's command runs only `tests/tools/test_cf_tools.py`. The break first appears at Task 9.2's full-suite run, with no task owning the fix.
- **What it contradicts:** the Sequencing claim "Each task leaves the suite green" (task file line 55) and Task 6's commit landing on a red suite (line 220).
- **Fix:** add a step to Task 6 that updates both pins and renames the first test. Derive the expected set from the `cf_tools` and `builtin` name constants, and replace `== 3` with `len(tools.list_tools())`. Add `uv run pytest tests/tools -q` as Task 6's scoped command.
- **Stale docs in the same step:** the package docstring "registers the built-in tools and does nothing else" (`src/squadron/tools/__init__.py:3-4`) and the comment at `src/squadron/pipeline/steps/utils.py:66-68` both become wrong.

findings.title: The protocol/transport failure row has no test, and the obvious implementation lets it escape
findings.description:
- **Gap against the design:** design lines 146 and 149-150 require a test for every failure-mode row, including "Protocol/transport error mid-call (`McpError`, closed stream)". Task 5.4 (lines 174-176) lists only timeout, server `isError` and spawn failure.
- **`test_unknown_tool_name` does not fill it:** the low-level MCP server turns a handler error into an ordinary `isError=True` result, so that test most likely repeats the `fail` test.
- **Why it matters in code:** `stdio_client` yields inside an `anyio` task group (`mcp/client/stdio/__init__.py:182-189`), and `ClientSession` opens a second one (`mcp/shared/session.py:221-238`). anyio 4.12 re-raises any body exception as `BaseExceptionGroup`. An `McpError` from `initialize()` or `call_tool()` therefore reaches the bridge as a nested `ExceptionGroup`.
- **Effect of Task 4.3 as written:** a plain `except McpError:` (line 143, "each `except` clause is specific") will not match. The exception leaves `call_mcp_tool` and is caught only by the loop's catch-all, which returns a generic "raised an unexpected exception". That violates fact 2 and the design row's WARNING signal.
- **This is also the realistic "spawn fails" case:** only a missing binary raises plain `OSError` before the task group (`stdio/__init__.py:131-137`), which is all Task 5.3 tests. "Package fetch fails" means `npx` starts and then exits, giving `McpError("Connection closed")` wrapped in a group.
- **Fix:**
  - Add a `crash` tool to the Task 3 fixture that exits the process mid-call.
  - Add a server-exits-before-initialize case, for example `command=sys.executable, args=["-c", "raise SystemExit(1)"]`.
  - Assert `is_error is True` plus the WARNING for both.
  - State in Task 4.3 that SDK errors arrive wrapped in `ExceptionGroup`, so the handler needs `except*` or group unwrapping.
  - Drop `test_unknown_tool_name`, or make it assert which path it exercises.

findings.title: Config read at execute time can raise out of the executor, and its shape conflicts with existing convention
findings.description:
Task 6.3 (lines 205-207) reads `cf.mcp_command` and `cf.mcp_timeout_s` inside the async executor and passes them to `shlex.split` and `StdioServerParameters`. Nothing in Tasks 6 or 7 handles these cases:

- `get_typed_config` raises `ValueError` on a non-int value (`manager.py:103-105`).
- `_read_toml` raises `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError` on a malformed file (`manager.py:46-51`).
- `shlex.split` raises `ValueError` on an unbalanced quote.
- An empty command gives `[]`, so indexing the command raises `IndexError`.

Each is a "command misconfigured" case. Design line 143 says that must return an `is_error=True` result explaining the bridge is unavailable, with a WARNING naming the launch command. As written they raise, against fact 2.

Three related gaps in the same step:

- **Blocking I/O:** execute-time reads do two synchronous TOML reads on the event loop per call. `agent.py:97-99` deliberately avoids this ("so that no config file I/O happens inside an async turn"). Design line 188 allows "factory/execute time", and the factory is synchronous.
- **Which directory:** the task does not say what `cwd` to pass to `get_config`. The default `"."` reads the process directory's `.squadron.toml`, not the bound one.
- **Typing:** `get_typed_config` returns `int | float`. Existing callers wrap it in `int(...)` (`events/dispatcher.py:92`), and strict pyright needs the same for `timeout_s: int`.

Fix: specify where config is read, pass `cwd=str(bound_cwd)`, convert the four errors to a result plus WARNING, and add one Task 7 test with a misconfigured command.

findings.title: The live contract test's "CI without node" premise is false for this repo
findings.description:
CI installs Node 22, installs `@context-forge/cli`, runs `cf init --lite --no-ide`, then runs `uv run pytest`. The Task 8.1 gate (lines 256-259) will find `npx -y @context-forge/mcp` launchable, so the test runs on every CI job in both matrix legs.

- **CI now depends on the npm registry** and on whatever unpinned CF release is current. An unrelated PR can go red on a CF release or a registry outage.
- **Task 8.2 runs in CI too:** "non-error content mentioning the project" (lines 266-268) has to hold in a runner checkout initialised with `cf init --lite`. That is unverified, and "mentioning the project" is not a checkable assertion as written.
- **No `network` marker:** the repo already has one (`pyproject.toml:83-85`), and the task does not apply it despite the design's own cold-start risk (design lines 273-275).
- **The gate runs at collection:** a module-level launch spawns `npx` on every full-suite collection, including `--collect-only` and `-k` runs, with no stated timeout.

Fix: move the gate into a module-scoped fixture bounded by `cf.mcp_timeout_s`, mark the module `network`, and state the intended CI behaviour. Either accept and document the live run, or have CI deselect it. Give 8.2 a concrete assertion.

findings.title: Tests and walkthrough steps can write to the real user config with no restore
findings.description:
- **Task 7.3 (lines 241-243)** says "with `cf.mcp_command` set to a multi-word value" without naming `patch_config_paths`. `set_config` without that fixture writes `~/.config/squadron/config.toml` (`manager.py:129-136`), and no plan command restores it.
- **Tasks 6 and 7 executors** read the developer's real user config at execute time unless the fixture is used. "Green with no network and no node" then also depends on local config.
- **Task 8's criterion "forcing an unlaunchable command skips rather than fails"** (lines 271-272) names no mechanism and no cleanup. A module-level gate cannot be reached by a per-test fixture, so the likely route is `sq config set` on the user config.
- **Task 9.1 step 3** uses `sq config set` then `unset` on the user config. `unset` deletes the key, so a local-dev override set earlier (the design's own example, lines 164-165) is lost, not restored.
- **A leftover bad value hides itself:** the Task 8 gate skips, so Task 9.2's "full suite green" passes with the contract unverified.

Fix: name `patch_config_paths` in Tasks 2 and 7. Give Task 8 a patched-config skip test. In 9.1, record the prior value with `sq config get` and re-set it afterwards, and add a `sq config get cf.mcp_command` check before 9.2.

findings.title: Two of the four result-mapping rules have no test
findings.description:
Success criterion 2 (design lines 221-222) requires results mapped "per the Result mapping rules". Task 5.1 covers `isError` and the no-text-block rule. It does not cover:

- joining multiple `TextContent` blocks with `\n` (design line 132); `echo` returns one block.
- noting non-text blocks by type (design line 137); the Task 3 fixture has no tool that returns one.

Task 4.2 implements both rules untested. Fix: add one fixture tool returning two text blocks plus an image block, and one test asserting the joined text and the type note.

findings.title: No executor-level round-trip against the fake server
findings.description:
Success criterion 3 (design lines 223-225) reads "against the fake python MCP server, an executor returns the server's text". Task 5 tests `call_mcp_tool` directly, and Task 7 tests executors with the transport mocked.

The seam between them is exercised only by Task 8.2, which is gated. That seam is config → `shlex.split` → `StdioServerParameters(cwd=bound_cwd)` → real spawn. A wrong `cwd` or argument split passes every ungated test.

Fix: give the fake server a `workflow_status` tool that returns its `os.getcwd()`. Add one Task 7 test that points `cf.mcp_command` at it via `patch_config_paths` and asserts the returned directory equals the bound one. This also verifies the Security claim at design lines 174-177.

findings.title: Success criterion 6's model-driven half has no executing task, yet the slice is marked complete
findings.description:
Criterion 6 (design lines 229-231) requires a dispatch where a tool-capable non-SDK model calls `cf_build_context`. Task 9.3 (lines 289-292) marks the task file and slice design `status: complete` while noting step 4 "remains open".

- **The guard is real but narrow:** it lives only in the `sq run` CLI path (`run.py:148`). A script that builds `OpenAICompatibleAgent` with `allowed_tools=["cf_workflow_status", "cf_build_context"]` is not blocked, the same way walkthrough step 2 bypasses the CLI.
- **Precedent:** slice 263 was closed the same way, with the open item recorded in the slice plan entry (`260-slices…md:51`).
- **Missing from 9.3:** it does not say where the open item is recorded, and it does not update the 264 entry in the slice plan (`260-slices…md:53`, still `[ ]`).

Fix: add a 9.1 step that drives the agent directly for criterion 6, or name the slice-plan entry as the place the open item is recorded.

findings.title: Task 5.2's timeout test needs fixture features Task 3 lacks, and its timing bound is too tight
findings.description:
- **PID capture:** Task 5.2 (lines 167-169) asserts the child is gone via a PID the fake server writes to a temp file. Task 3.1 specifies no such behaviour, so Task 5 has to rework the committed fixture. Since an explicit `env` is only merged over the default whitelist (`stdio/__init__.py:127`), the simplest route is a `--pid-file` argument, specified in Task 3.
- **Timing:** "within ~timeout wall-clock" (line 166) is not what the SDK does. After cancellation, teardown waits up to 2s for exit (`stdio/__init__.py:48, 202-209`), then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 more. A blocking `sleep` tool returns at about timeout + 2s. State the bound as timeout + about 5s.
- **Overclaim:** the task says the assertion "pins the SDK process-group teardown fact". The fake server has no grandchild, so a direct-child check would pass without `killpg`. Either have `sleep` spawn a child and assert both are gone, or drop the claim. The design (lines 156-157) only requires the direct-child check.

findings.title: Task count is heavier than a 2/5 slice needs
findings.description:
The design rates the slice 2/5 (design line 335). The plan has nine tasks, four of them rated 3/5.

- **Merge Tasks 1 and 2:** two config entries plus two default assertions is one task and one commit. The existing pattern is `tests/config/test_keys.py:51-85`.
- **Fold Task 3 into Task 5:** the fixture has no consumer until then. Its "by hand" check (lines 118-119) and Task 4's "manual smoke" (line 151) both duplicate `test_echo_round_trip`.
- **Replace `test_unknown_tool_name`** (lines 162-163): it traces to no success criterion.

findings.title: Env handling in Tasks 4.1 and 6.3 is redundant and self-contradictory
findings.description: Task 4.1 (lines 129-131) says the bridge uses `get_default_environment()` and, in the same bullet, that callers build the parameters. Task 6.3 passes `env=get_default_environment()`. The SDK already applies that environment when `env` is `None` and merges it under any explicit one (`mcp/client/stdio/__init__.py:127`). Both steps are no-ops; delete them.

findings.title: Task 7.4 misstates the `validate_allowed_tools` signature
findings.description: The function takes `(config: StepConfig, action_type: str)`, not a list of names as lines 244-245 imply. The test needs a `StepConfig` built like the `_step` helper in `tests/pipeline/steps/test_allowed_tools_validation.py:10-11`. That file is also the natural home for the test.

findings.title: Commit instructions are checkbox items, and two land before tests
findings.description: The file has no `**Commit**:` marker lines, which is acceptable. Commits appear as checkboxes in every task's success criteria. The per-task cadence follows `CLAUDE.md:36`. Task 4's commit precedes any automated test, and Task 6's lands on the red suite from the FAIL finding. Merging the implementation and test pairs would put every commit at a tested point.

findings.title: The plan relies on mcp 1.26.0 behaviour while the dependency floor is `mcp>=1.0.0`
findings.description: Fact 6 forbids custom kill code on the strength of SDK behaviour verified at 1.26.0, the version `uv.lock` pins. The published floor permits older SDKs. This is also the first import of `mcp` anywhere in `src/` or `tests/`. Consider raising the floor in Task 1.
